claims.claim: Replacing sugar-containing, acidic drinks, such as soft drinks (typically 8-12 g sugars/100 ml), with reformulated drinks contributes to the maintenance of tooth mineralisation.

conditions.info: In order to bear the claim, reformulated acidic drinks shall comply with the description of the food subject to the claim.

claims.claim: Consumption of foods/drinks containing <name of all used non-fermentable carbohydrates> instead of fermentable carbohydrates contributes to the maintenance of tooth mineralisation.

requirements.replacement: Fermentable carbohydrates should be replaced in foods or drinks by non-fermentable carbohydrates.
requirements.pH_limit: Consumption of such foods or drinks must not lower plaque pH below 5.7 during and up to 30 minutes after consumption.

definitions.fermentable_carbohydrates: Carbohydrates or carbohydrate mixtures as consumed in foods or beverages that lower plaque pH below 5.7, as determined in vivo or in situ by plaque pH telemetry tests, by bacterial fermentation during and up to 30 minutes after consumption.
definitions.non_fermentable_carbohydrates: Carbohydrates or carbohydrate mixtures as consumed in foods or beverages that do not lower plaque pH, as determined in vivo or in situ by plaque pH telemetry tests, below a conservative value of 5.7 by bacterial fermentation during and up to 30 minutes after consumption.

nutrient: A combination of artichoke leaf dry extract standardised in caffeoylquinic acids, monacolin K in red yeast rice, sugar-cane derived policosanols, procyanidolic oligomers from French maritime pine bark, garlic dry extract standardised in allicin, d-α-tocopheryl hydrogen succinate, riboflavin and inositol hexanicotinate

claims.claim: A combination of artichoke leaf dry extract standardised in caffeoylquinic acids, monacolin K in red yeast rice, sugar-cane derived policosanols, procyanidolic oligomers from French maritime pine bark, garlic dry extract standardised in allicin, d-α-tocopheryl hydrogen succinate, riboflavin and inositol hexanicotinate reduces blood LDL-cholesterol concentrations. High LDL-cholesterol is a risk factor in the development of coronary heart disease.

conditions.consumption_recommendation: Divided into three daily doses to be consumed with the major meals.

claims.claim: Activated charcoal contributes to reducing excessive flatulence after eating.

conditions.info: The claim may be used only for food which contains 1 g of activated charcoal per quantified portion. In order to bear the claim, information shall be given to the consumer that the beneficial effect is obtained with 1 g, which should be taken at least 30 minutes before and 1 g shortly after the meal.

claims.claim: Consumption of alpha-cyclodextrin as part of a starch-containing meal contributes to the reduction of the blood glucose rise after that meal.

conditions.info: The claim may be used for food which contains at least 5 g of alpha-cyclodextrin per 50 g of starch in a quantified portion as part of the meal. In order to bear the claim, information shall be given to the consumer that the beneficial effect is obtained by consuming the alpha-cyclodextrin as part of the meal.

claims.claim: ALA contributes to the maintenance of normal blood cholesterol levels.

conditions.info: The claim may be used only for food which is at least a source of ALA as referred to in the claim SOURCE OF OMEGA 3 FATTY ACIDS as listed in the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006. Information shall be given to the consumer that the beneficial effect is obtained with a daily intake of 2 g of ALA.

claims.claim: Consumption of arabinoxylan as part of a meal contributes to a reduction of the blood glucose rise after that meal.

conditions.info: The claim may be used only for food which contains at least 8 g of arabinoxylan (AX)-rich fibre produced from wheat endosperm (at least 60 % AX by weight) per 100 g of available carbohydrates in a quantified portion as part of the meal. In order to bear the claim, information shall be given to the consumer that the beneficial effect is obtained by consuming the arabinoxylan (AX)-rich fibre produced from wheat endosperm as part of the meal.

claims.claim: Substituting one daily meal of an energy restricted diet with a meal replacement contributes to the maintenance of weight after weight loss

conditions.reference_regulation: Energy and protein requirements, WHO/FAO/UNU Meeting, WHO Technical Report Series 724
conditions.info: In order to bear the claim, a food should comply with the following requirements: 1. Energy content shall not be less than 200 kcal (840 kJ) and shall not exceed 250 kcal (1046 KJ) per meal. 2. Fat content and composition: Energy derived from fat shall not exceed 30% of total available energy. Linoleic acid (in the form of glycerides) shall not be less than 1 g. 3. Protein content and composition: The protein contained in the food shall provide not less than 25% and not more than 50% of the total energy content. The chemical index of protein shall be equal to that set by the WHO in ‘Energy and protein requirements’ (1985, WHO Technical Report Series 724). If the chemical index is lower than 100% of the reference protein, the minimum protein levels shall be correspondingly increased. In any case, the chemical index of the protein shall at least be equal to 80% of that of the reference protein. 4. Vitamins and minerals: The food shall provide at least 30% of the nutrient reference values per meal as laid down in Annex XIII to Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, except for fluoride, chromium, chloride, and molybdenum. The amount of sodium per meal shall be at least 172.5 mg, and potassium at least 500 mg. Information shall be provided to the consumer on the importance of maintaining an adequate daily fluid intake and that the products are useful only as part of an energy-restricted diet.

claims.claim: Substituting two daily meals of an energy restricted diet with meal replacements contributes to weight loss

conditions.info: In order to bear the claim, a food should comply with the following requirements: 1. Energy content shall be between 200 kcal (840 kJ) and 250 kcal (1046 kJ) per meal. 2. Fat content and composition: Energy from fat shall not exceed 30% of total energy content. Linoleic acid (in glycerides) shall be at least 1 g. 3. Protein content and composition: Protein shall provide between 25% and 50% of total energy. The chemical index of protein must meet WHO standards. 4. Vitamins and minerals: The food shall provide at least 30% of the nutrient reference values per meal as per Annex XIII to Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, except fluoride, chromium, chloride, and molybdenum. Sodium content shall be at least 172.5 mg per meal, and potassium at least 500 mg.
